overriding-and-specialization.label: Overriding and Specialization
overriding-and-specialization.summary: Override inherited behavior by keeping the same public method name while a subclass supplies a more specific implementation.

try_overriding_and_specialization_sketch.title: Override label() on Book
try_overriding_and_specialization_sketch.prompt: `Book` already inherits from `CatalogItem`, and `main.py` is complete. In `models/book.py`, override the inherited `label(self)` method so a `Book` returns `Book: ` followed by that object's title. Keep the method name `label`, keep `Book` inheriting from `CatalogItem`, and leave `models/catalog_item.py` and `main.py` unchanged.
try_overriding_and_specialization_sketch.hint: Define `label(self)` inside `Book`. The child method should use `self.title` and return the specialized text.

help.concept: An override uses the same method name as the inherited method but provides subclass-specific behavior.

try_overriding_and_specialization_sketch.starterCode:
from models.book import Book

title = input()
book = Book(title)

print(book.label())

main_py.content:
from models.book import Book

title = input()
book = Book(title)

print(book.label())

models_book_py.content:
from models.catalog_item import CatalogItem


class Book(CatalogItem):
    # Override label() here.
    pass

sc-overriding-purpose.title: Why override an inherited method?
sc-overriding-purpose.prompt: `CatalogItem.label()` returns only the title. Why should `Book` override `label()` instead of inventing a different method name?
sc-overriding-purpose.hint: The caller should keep using the same public behavior.

help.concept: Overriding preserves the inherited method contract while allowing the subclass to specialize its implementation.
help.hint_2: The child can return a more specific result.

options.b: To force callers to learn a new method name for every subclass
options.c: To keep the `label()` contract while giving `Book` book-specific behavior
options.d: To remove the title state inherited from `CatalogItem`

fb-overriding-method-name.title: Keep the inherited method name
fb-overriding-method-name.prompt: Complete the method name so `Book` overrides the method it inherits from `CatalogItem`.
fb-overriding-method-name.hint: An override uses the same method name as the parent.

help.concept: Python recognizes the subclass implementation as an override because it uses the same method name.

sc-overriding-shared-contract.title: Which label() runs?
sc-overriding-shared-contract.prompt: `CatalogItem.label()` returns `self.title`, while `Book.label()` returns `Book: ` plus the title. What does `Book("Coraline").label()` return?
sc-overriding-shared-contract.hint: Python looks on the subclass before falling back to the parent.

help.concept: When a subclass overrides a method, calls on that subclass use the subclass implementation.

options.d: Python raises an error because both classes define `label()`

catalog-step-book-and-movie.title: Specialize labels for two catalog subclasses
catalog-step-book-and-movie.prompt: You are extending a media catalog. The base `CatalogItem` already stores `title`. Complete both subclasses so they reuse the parent constructor and override `display_name()`: `BookItem` should return `"<title> by <author>"`, and `MovieItem` should return `"<title> (<minutes> min)"`. The workspace already includes a small `main.py` that prints both labels.
catalog-step-book-and-movie.hint: Both subclasses share the same method name, but each one formats the result differently.

help.concept: Different subclasses can override the same base method in different ways while still fitting the same base-class contract.
help.hint_1: Use `super().__init__(title)` in both subclass constructors before storing the extra field.
help.hint_2: Write one `display_name()` method in each subclass, each returning its own specialized string format.

movie = MovieItem("Arrival", 116)
print(book.display_name())
print(movie.display_name())

catalog-step-mixed-report.title: Build a report from mixed specialized items
catalog-step-mixed-report.prompt: Build a mixed catalog report without checking object types manually. The workspace includes a base `CatalogItem` plus `BookItem` and `MovieItem` subclasses that all provide `display_name()`. Complete `build_display_report(items)` in `services/reporting.py` so it returns each item's display label in order. `main.py` will print the returned lines.
catalog-step-mixed-report.hint: Loop through the mixed list and call the same `display_name()` method on every item.

help.concept: Polymorphic services work by calling the same method on mixed related objects, while overriding lets each subclass provide its own specialized output.
help.hint_1: Make sure each subclass overrides `display_name()` correctly before writing the service loop.
help.hint_2: In the service function, iterate through `items` and append `item.display_name()` for each object in order.

catalog-step-mixed-report.starterCode:
from models.catalog_item import CatalogItem
from models.book_item import BookItem
from models.movie_item import MovieItem
from services.reporting import build_display_report

items = [
    CatalogItem("Notebook"),
    BookItem("Refactoring", "Martin Fowler"),
    MovieItem("Up", 96),
]
for line in build_display_report(items):
    print(line)

practice-specialized-display-label.title: Override a display label in one subclass
practice-specialized-display-label.prompt: Define a base class `MediaItem` that stores `title` and has `display()` returning `Item: <title>`. Define `Song(MediaItem)` and override `display()` so it returns `Song: <title>`. Print the display text for one base item and one song.
practice-specialized-display-label.hint: Keep the shared version on the base class, then redefine only `display()` inside `Song`.

help.concept: Overriding lets a subclass specialize one inherited behavior while keeping the rest of the shared base-class structure.
help.hint_1: Keep the shared version on the base class, then redefine only `display()` inside `Song`.
help.hint_2: Run the program and compare the output with the expected example.
